So Allah seals their mouths and they cannot deny. Allah makes other limbs speak besides their tongues, and they confess their sins.

The second: When Allah says to them, ﴿Did I not charge you﴾, they have no answer. So they fall silent and become mute, and their limbs other than the tongue speak. Regarding the sealing of the mouths, there are several views:

The strongest of them is that Allah silences their tongues so they cannot speak with them, and makes their limbs speak so they bear witness against them. This is easy in Allah's power. Silencing is clearly possible. As for making the limbs speak, the tongue is a organ that moves by a specific motion, so just as it can move by it, other organs can move by a similar motion, and Allah is capable of all possibilities.

Another view is that they say nothing, because their excuses are cut off and their coverings are torn away. So they stand with heads bowed, standing in the manner of one who is despairing and hopeless. No one finds an excuse to offer, and there is no room for repentance to seek forgiveness. The speaking of the hands is the manifestation of matters to such a degree that denial is no longer possible, even to the point that the hands and eyes speak of it, as the saying goes: "The walls weep for the owner of the house," indicating the appearance of grief.

The first view is the correct one, and it contains verbal and semantic subtleties.

As for the verbal subtleties, the first is this: Allah attributed the act of sealing to Himself, saying ﴿We seal﴾, and attributed speech and testimony to the hands and feet. This is because if He had said, ﴿We seal upon their mouths﴾ and "their hands speak," there would be the possibility that this was from them under compulsion and force, and admission under compulsion is not accepted. So He said, ﴿and their hands speak to Us and their feet bear witness﴾, meaning by their own choice after Allah empowers them to speak, so that it is more indicative of the sin proceeding from them.

The second: Allah said, ﴿and their hands speak to Us and their feet bear witness﴾, assigning the testimony to the feet and the speech to the hands. This is because actions are attributed to the hands. Allah said, ﴿and what their hands made﴾ (36:35), meaning what they did, and He said, ﴿and do not cast yourselves by your own hands﴾ (2:195), meaning do not cast yourselves. So the hands are as the doers, and the witness against the doer should be other than him. Thus He made the feet and skins among the witnesses, because the attribution of actions to them is remote.

As for the semantic subtleties, the first is this: On the Day of Resurrection, every witness whose testimony is accepted, from among the close ones and the truthful, are all enemies of the criminals, and the testimony of an enemy against an enemy is not accepted. Even if the witnesses are upright, the disbelievers and transgressors who are not truthful are not acceptable as witnesses. So Allah made the witness against them be from among themselves. It may be objected that the hands and feet also committed sins, so they are transgressors and their testimony should not be accepted. We say: rejecting their testimony is itself accepting it. If they lie on that day, then the sin has come from them on that day, and the one who sins on that day, with the matters manifest, must have been sinful in the world. If they tell the truth on that day, then the sin came from them in the world. This is like one who says to a transgressor: "If you lie during the daytime of this day, then my slave is free." The transgressor says: "I lied during the daytime of this day." The slave is freed, because if he speaks truthfully in saying "I lied during the daytime of this day," then the condition has been met and the consequence is due. If he lies in saying "I lied," then he lied during the daytime of that day, so the condition has also been met. This is unlike if he said on the second day, "I lied during the daytime of the day on which you attached the freeing of your slave to my lie."

The second issue: The sealing applies to the disbelievers in this world upon their hearts, and in the Hereafter upon their mouths. At the time the sealing was upon their hearts, their speech was with their mouths, as He says, ﴿That is their saying with their mouths﴾ (9:30). When their mouths were sealed as well, it follows that their speech would be with their limbs, because a person owns nothing except the heart, the tongue, and the limbs. When the heart and the mouth no longer remain, the limbs and the members become specified.

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if We willed, We would have obliterated their eyes, so they would race to the path; but how could they see?﴾ ﴿And if We willed, We would have transformed them in their places, so they would be unable to proceed, nor could they return.﴾

We have mentioned repeatedly that the straight path (al-sirat al-mustaqim) lies between compulsion (al-jabr) and free will (al-qadar), and it is the middle way (al-tariqah al-wusta). God, exalted is He, in every place where He mentions what the Compulsionists (al-mujabbirah) hold to, mentions after it what the Qadariyyah hold to, and vice versa. Here too it is so: when God, exalted is He, said, ﴿And their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn﴾ and said, ﴿Burn therein today for what you used to disbelieve﴾, and this was the Qadariyyah's hold, since God attributed disbelief and earning to them and ascribed good and evil to them, He mentioned after it what indicates that their disbelief and their earning are by the will of God. This is because disbelief blinds insight and weakens the rational faculty, and the blinding of insight is by the will and volition of God: when He wills, He blinds the insights, just as, if He willed, He would obliterate their seeing eyes and deprive them of the rational faculty by His choice and will, just as the deprivation of physical strength is by His will. Even if He willed, He would transform the responsible person in his place and make him stand such that he could not move right or left, nor be able to advance or return. So the blinding of insights in His sight is like the blinding of eyes, and the deprivation of the rational faculty is like the deprivation of physical strength. Thus He said, ﴿And if We willed, We would have obliterated their eyes﴾, as an indication that if He willed and wished to blind their insights, they would go astray; and that if He willed to obliterate their eyes, they would not have been guided to their apparent path; and that if He willed and chose to deprive their minds of strength, they would stumble; and that if He willed to deprive their bodies of strength and transform them, they would not be able to advance or retreat. In the two verses there are linguistic discussions:

The first discussion: concerning His words, ﴿so they would race to the path﴾. Al-Zamakhshari said: In it there are several aspects.

The first: that it contains the omission of the preposition "ila" (to) and the verb being connected without a preposition, its original form being "fa-istabaqu ila al-sirat" (so they would race to the path).

The second: that the intended meaning of "istibaq" is "ibtidar" (hastening), so he made it operate as "ibtidar" operates.

The third: one may make the path the one racing, not the one raced to; it is said "istabaqna fa-sabaqtuhum" (we raced and I outdistanced them). In that case it is an intensification in being guided to the way, as if he says: the path which is with them, they are not seeking it nor intending it; rather they are upon it, and when God obliterates their eyes they do not see it, so how much more if they were not upon the path.

The second discussion: He placed the obliteration and blinding before the transformation and incapacitation, so that the speech would be graduated, as if He said: if He blinds them, they will not see the way they are on, and then they will not be guided to it. If someone says: the blind may be guided to the path by rational or sensory signs other than sight, such as sounds and walking by the sense of touch, so [Zamakhshari] advanced and said: if He transforms them and deprives their strength entirely, they will not be guided to the path by any means whatsoever.

The third discussion: He placed "proceeding" (mudiyy) before "returning" (ruju'), because returning is easier than proceeding; for proceeding does not indicate having traveled the way before, whereas returning does indicate it, and there is no doubt that traveling a path already seen once is easier than traveling a path not seen. So He said, ﴿but they could not proceed (mudiyyan)﴾ [Ya-Sin: 67], and not even the least of that, which is returning, which is easier than proceeding.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whomsoever We grant long life, We reverse him in creation. Do they not then understand?﴾

We have already mentioned that His saying, ﴿Did I not charge you﴾, is a cutting off of excuses by means of the prior warning. Then, once He had established this and completed it, He moved on to cutting off another excuse, namely that the disbeliever says: "Our remaining in the world was but brief, and if You had granted us long life, You would not have found any shortcoming in us." So Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Do they not then understand?﴾ Indeed, every time you advance in years you grow weaker, and We have already granted you life long enough for you to be able to reflect and comprehend. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Did We not grant you a life long enough for whoever would take heed to take heed therein?﴾ [Fatir: 37]. Moreover, you know that the more time passes over you, the more your weakness increases, so you squandered the time of possibility (zaman al-imkan, the time in which action is possible). Had We granted you more than that, there would have followed it the time of incapacity (zaman al-izman, the time of inability to act), and whoever does not perform the obligatory act in the time of possibility would not perform it in the time of incapacity.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 36, verse 69–70:

There are two views regarding the order.

We have already mentioned that in every passage where God mentions two of the three foundations (usul) — the Oneness (tawhid), the Prophethood (risalah) and the Resurrection (hashr) — He mentions the third of them. Here He mentions two: the Oneness and the Resurrection. As for the Oneness, it is in His saying, ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan﴾, and in His saying, ﴿and that you should worship Me; this is a straight path﴾. As for the Resurrection, it is in His saying, ﴿Burn therein today﴾, and in His saying, ﴿Today We shall seal their mouths﴾, and other than these. So when He mentioned them and clarified them, He mentioned the third foundation, which is the Prophethood, saying: ﴿We did not teach him poetry, nor is it fitting for him. It is only a reminder and a clear Qur'an﴾. His saying, ﴿We did not teach him poetry﴾, is an indication that he is taught by God: He taught him what He willed and did not teach him what He did not will. There are several discussions concerning the interpretation of the verse:

The first discussion: Poetry is singled out for the negation of teaching, although the disbelievers used to attribute to the Prophet (ﷺ) various things, among which was sorcery (sihr), and He did not say, "We did not teach him sorcery." Likewise they attributed to him soothsaying (kihanah), and He did not say, "We did not teach him soothsaying." We say: As for soothsaying, they attributed the Prophet (ﷺ) to it when he informed of the unseen and it came about as he said.

As for sorcery, they attributed it to him when he did what others were unable to do, such as splitting the moon, the speaking of pebbles and the trunk, and other things.

As for poetry, they attributed it to him when he recited the Qur'an to them. However, he (ﷺ) did not challenge except with the Qur'an, as God, the Exalted, said:

Page 92
﴿And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant, then produce a surah like it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 23], and so on. He did not say: "If you are in doubt about my prophethood, then make the trunks speak, or feed the great multitude, or inform of the unseen." Since his challenge (ﷺ) was with speech, and they attributed him to poetry when speaking, poetry was singled out for the negation of teaching.

The second discussion: What is the meaning of His saying, ﴿nor is it fitting for him﴾? We say: Some people said: it was not possible for him. Others said: it was not easy for him, to the extent that if he quoted a line of poetry, it was heard from him deficient in meter. It is narrated that he (ﷺ) used to say: "And there will come to you one who has not been provided with news."

There is a better view than this, namely that "what is fitting for him" be taken in its apparent sense: that poetry was not becoming for him and not suitable for him. This is because poetry leads to altering the meaning for the sake of observing the wording and the meter. The speaker's wording follows the meaning, whereas the poet's meaning follows the wording: he intends a word with which the meter or rhyme of the poem is correct, and so he needs to contrive a meaning that he brings for the sake of that word. On this basis we say: poetry is speech that is metrical, the meter of which is intended as a primary aim. As for one who intends the meaning and it comes out metrical and rhymed, he is not a poet. Do you not see that His saying, ﴿You will not attain righteousness until you spend from what you love﴾ [Al 'Imran: 92], is not poetry? A poet, when speech issues from him containing moving and still letters in the same number as this verse, scanned as fa'ilatun fa'ilatun, it becomes poetry, because he intended to bring words whose letters are moving and still in that way, and the meaning followed it. The wise person intended the meaning and it came in those words. On this basis the answer is obtained to the one who says that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited a line of poetry, which is his saying:

I am the Prophet, no lie; I am the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib.
Or two lines. We say that this is not poetry, because he did not intend the meter and the rhyme. On this basis, if many metrical and rhymed statements issued from the Prophet (ﷺ), they would not be poetry, because he did not intend the wording as a primary aim. This is confirmed by what we have mentioned: if you survey people's speech in the markets, you find in it what is metrical and falls within one of the meters of poetry, yet the speaker is not called a poet and the speech is not called poetry, due to the absence of primary intent toward the wording.

Then His saying, ﴿It is only a reminder and a clear Qur'an﴾ confirms this meaning, i.e., it is a reminder and an admonition, as the intent is toward the meaning. Poetry is a wording embellished with rhyme and meter. Here there is a subtle point:

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, some poetry contains wisdom." That is: a poet may intend a wording, and a wise meaning happens to match it, just as the wise person may intend a meaning, and a poetic meter happens to match it. But the wise person does not become a poet by reason of that meter, whereas the poet may become wise by reason of that remembrance, since the Prophet (ﷺ) called his poetry wisdom, while God negated that the Prophet was a poet. This is because the wording is the mold of the meaning, and the meaning is the heart of the wording and its spirit. When the heart is present, one does not look at the mold. Thus the wise person's speech, though metrical, remains wise, and the meter of his speech does not take it out of wisdom. And the admonishing poet's speech is wise.

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿That he may warn whoever is alive, and that the word may be fulfilled against the disbelievers.﴾

It is read with the ta' (second person, "you") and with the ya' (third person). The ta' form addresses the Prophet ﷺ. With the ya' there are two possibilities:

The first: the warner is the Prophet ﷺ, since his mention preceded in His saying: ﴿And We did not teach him (poetry)﴾ and His saying: ﴿nor is it befitting for him﴾.

The second: what is meant is that the Qur'an warns. The first is closer to the meaning, and the second is closer to the wording. As for the first, the attribute "warner" (mundhir) applies to the Messengers far more frequently than to the Books; as for the second, the Qur'an is the nearest of the two mentioned to His saying: ﴿that he may warn﴾.

His saying: ﴿whoever is alive﴾ means: whoever is living of heart. It admits of two interpretations:

The first: what is meant is whoever is alive in God's knowledge, so that he is warned by it and believes.

The second: what is meant is that he may warn thereby whoever is alive in reality, that is, whoever believes; he warns them of the punishment for sins and of the reward for obedience. ﴿And that the word may be fulfilled against the disbelievers.﴾ As for the word of punishment and its decree, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿But the word from Me has come into effect: I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together﴾ [al-Sajdah: 13], and His saying: ﴿The word of punishment has been fulfilled﴾ [al-Zumar: 71]. This is because God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We never punish until We have sent a Messenger﴾ [al-Isra': 15]. So when the Messenger comes, the punishment becomes due upon whoever was found to have denied. As for the spoken word concerning the Oneness (of God), the Prophethood, the Gathering (of the dead), and the rest of the fundamental religious questions, the Qur'an contains the mention of the proofs by which the objectives are established.

Then He, exalted is He, repeated the Oneness and the proofs indicating it, and said: ﴿Do they not see that We have created for them, of what Our hands have wrought, cattle, and they are their owners?﴾

That is: of what Our hands have wrought, i.e., what We made without any helper or assistant, but made by Our power and will.

His saying: ﴿and they are their owners﴾ is an indication of the completion of the blessing in the creation of cattle, for if He had created them without making them owned by man, man would not benefit from them.

His saying: ﴿And We have made them subservient to them﴾ is an additional blessing, for a possessed animal that is refractory and rebellious is of no use. If man owned cattle that were unruly and resistant, the blessing of riding would not be complete, and eating would be obtained only as among wild animals; indeed, the blessing of eating would not be perfected except with the toil of hunting, and perhaps that is not available to everyone.

His saying: ﴿So some of them they ride, and some of them they eat﴾ explains the benefit of subjugation, for were it not for subjugation, one of the two benefits would not exist and the other would be rare.

Then He, exalted is He, explained benefits other than riding and eating by His saying: ﴿And for them in them are benefits and drinks﴾. This is because among animals there are some that are not ridden, such as sheep; so He said "benefits" to encompass them. The "drinks" are likewise general, if we say that what is meant is the plural of mishrab, which is a vessel, for some hides are made into vessels for drinking and into utensils such as waterskins [and others]. And if we say that what is meant is the drink itself, namely milk and fat, these are specific to females; yet this depends on males, for that is contingent upon pregnancy, which comes from both males and females.

Had you been thankful, He would have increased you of His bounty; had you disbelieved, He would have taken them away from you. So what is your saying: will you not give thanks, so as to sustain them and to be granted more of them?

The third: what they conceal of corrupt beliefs, and what they reveal of abominable deeds.

*Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 36, verses 77–80*

His saying, ﴿then behold, he is an open adversary﴾, contains a subtle and strange point. He, exalted is He, said: the variation in the forms of his limbs, despite the similarity of the parts of what he was created from, is a manifest sign. Yet there is something even more manifest, which is his speech and his understanding. This is because the drop (nutfah) is a body. Suppose an ignorant person says that it transformed and became another body. But from where does the drop bring the speaking faculty and the understanding faculty? The bringing into being of speech and understanding is more wondrous and stranger than the bringing into being of the form and the body, and it is closer to recognising power and choice.

So His saying, ﴿adversary﴾, means speaking. He mentioned "adversary" in place of "speaking" because it is the highest state of the speaker. A speaker with himself does not make his speech as clear as he does when he speaks with another. And one who speaks with another who is not an adversary does not make it as clear or exert himself as he does when his speech is directed at an opponent. His saying, ﴿open﴾, points to the strength of his intellect. He chose "clear" (ibanah) because the intelligent person, when he makes something understood, is of higher rank than when he is not, since the one who makes clear has first had the matter become clear to him, then he made it clear to others.

Thus His saying, ﴿from a drop﴾, indicates the lowest state he was in, and His saying, ﴿an open adversary﴾, indicates the highest state he attained. This is like His saying: ﴿Then We made the drop a clinging clot, then We made the clot a lump of flesh﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 14], up to His saying, ﴿then We developed him into another creation﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 14]. So what preceded, namely the making of the drop into a clot, the making of the clot into a lump, and the making of the lump into bones, indicates the changes in the body. And His saying, ﴿then We developed him into another creation﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 14], indicates what He pointed to with His saying, ﴿then behold, he is an open adversary﴾, that is, a speaking, intelligent being.

Then His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And he presents Us with a parable and forgets his own creation﴾, indicates the explanation of the gathering for resurrection (ḥashr). In these verses, up to the end of the surah, there are strange and wondrous matters, which we will mention as far as possible, God willing.

So we say: among those who deny the gathering for resurrection, some mention no proof or doubt and are content with mere disbelief in its likelihood (istib'ad), and claim that it is self-evident. These are the majority. This is indicated by His saying, exalted is He, relating about them in many places, in the language of disbelief in its likelihood, as He said: ﴿And they say: "When we are lost in the earth, shall we indeed be in a new creation?"﴾ [al-Sajdah: 10]; ﴿"When we die and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be raised?"﴾ [al-Saffat: 16]; ﴿"Are you indeed of those who believe?"﴾ [al-Saffat: 52]; ﴿"When we die and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be recompensed?"﴾ [al-Saffat: 53], and others besides these. So likewise here, He said: ﴿He says: "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?"﴾, in the manner of disbelief in its likelihood. So He first began by nullifying their disbelief in its likelihood with His saying: ﴿and forgets his own creation﴾, that is, forgets that We created him from dust and from a drop of similar parts.

[Page 96]

Then We made for them, from the forelocks to the feet, limbs of differing forms and structures. We were not content with that, but deposited in them what is not of the kind of these bodies, namely speech and intellect, by which they deserved honour. If they are content with mere disbelief in its likelihood, why do they not find it unlikely that a speaking, intelligent being was created from a foul drop which had never been a place of life at all? And they find it unlikely that speech and intellect could be returned to a place in which they had been. Furthermore, their disbelief in its likelihood was on account of the dispersal and scattering that occur in the afterlife, when they said: ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾ They chose the bone for the mention because it is furthest from life, since it lacks sensation, and they described it with what strengthens the side of their disbelief, namely decay and crumbling. But God repelled their disbelief in its likelihood by pointing to the power and knowledge of the One who restores, so He said: ﴿And He presents Us with a parable﴾, that is, He made Our power like their power, ﴿and forgets his own creation﴾, the wondrous creation and the strange beginning.

Among them are those who mention a doubt, even though at its end it returns to mere disbelief in its likelihood. It is of two kinds:

The first: that after non-existence, the person has become nothing, so how can existence be predicated of non-existence? He answered this doubt with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "He will give them life who produced them the first time."﴾ That is, just as He created man when he was not a thing worth mentioning, so He will restore him even if he no longer remains a thing worth mentioning.

The second: whoever's parts have been scattered in the eastern and western regions of the world, and some of him has become in the bodies of predatory beasts and some in the walls of buildings, how can he be gathered? Even more remote than this is that when one human eats another human and the parts of the eaten one become parts of the eater: if the eaten one is restored, then either its parts are returned to the body of the eater, and no parts remain for the eaten one from which its limbs could be created; or they are returned to the body of the eaten one, and no parts remain for the eater.

God, exalted is He, said in refuting this doubt: ﴿And He is Knowing of every creation﴾. Its meaning is that in the eater there are original parts and added parts, and likewise in the eaten. When one human eats another, the original parts of the eaten become added parts of the eater, while the original parts of the eater are those he had before eating. ﴿And God is Knowing of every creation﴾: He knows the original from the added, so He gathers the original parts of the eaten and breathes His spirit into them. Likewise He gathers the parts scattered in the dispersed places in the far corners, by His all-encompassing wisdom and His perfect power.

Then He, exalted is He, returned to establishing what preceded: the repelling of their disbelief in its likelihood and the nullifying of their denial and obstinacy.

*Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 36, verses 77–80*

His saying, ﴿then behold, he is an open adversary﴾, contains a subtle and strange point. He, exalted is He, said: the variation in the forms of his limbs, despite the similarity of the parts of what he was created from, is a manifest sign. Yet there is something even more manifest, which is his speech and his understanding. This is because the drop (nutfah) is a body. Suppose an ignorant person says that it transformed and became another body. But from where does the drop bring the speaking faculty and the understanding faculty? The bringing into being of speech and understanding is more wondrous and stranger than the bringing into being of the form and the body, and it is closer to recognising power and choice.

So His saying, ﴿adversary﴾, means speaking. He mentioned "adversary" in place of "speaking" because it is the highest state of the speaker. A speaker with himself does not make his speech as clear as he does when he speaks with another. And one who speaks with another who is not an adversary does not make it as clear or exert himself as he does when his speech is directed at an opponent. His saying, ﴿open﴾, points to the strength of his intellect. He chose "clear" (ibanah) because the intelligent person, when he makes something understood, is of higher rank than when he is not, since the one who makes clear has first had the matter become clear to him, then he made it clear to others.

Thus His saying, ﴿from a drop﴾, indicates the lowest state he was in, and His saying, ﴿an open adversary﴾, indicates the highest state he attained. This is like His saying: ﴿Then We made the drop a clinging clot, then We made the clot a lump of flesh﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 14], up to His saying, ﴿then We developed him into another creation﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 14]. So what preceded, namely the making of the drop into a clot, the making of the clot into a lump, and the making of the lump into bones, indicates the changes in the body. Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 36, verse 81–82:

Then He said, the Exalted: ﴿He who has made for you fire from the green tree, and behold, you kindle from it.﴾

Its meaning is that man comprises a body which he perceives and a life that flows within it, and this is like a heat that runs through it. If you find it strange that there is heat and life in him, then do not find it strange, for fire in the green tree, from which water drips, is more wondrous and more remarkable, and you are present where you kindle from it. And if you find the creation of his body strange, then the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of your selves, so do not find it strange, for Allah created the heavens and the earth. Thus the subtlety of His saying, the Exalted, becomes clear: ﴿He who has made for you fire from the green tree, and behold, you kindle from it.﴾

Page 97
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the like of them?﴾ The mention of fire in the tree is placed before the mention of the greater creation, because their disbelief was explicitly directed at the revival, when they said: ﴿Who will give life to the bones?﴾ and they did not say "who will gather them and put them together." And the fire in the tree is appropriate to life.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Yes, and He is the All-Creating, the All-Knowing﴾ is an indication that He is perfect in power.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ is an indication that His knowledge is all-encompassing.

Then He confirmed His explanation with His saying, the Exalted: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ This is a demonstration of the corruption of their comparison and likening and their coining of similitudes, for they coined a similitude for Allah and said: No one is able to do the like of this, analogizing the Unseen to the seen. So He said regarding the seen: creation occurs by bodily instruments and spatial movements, and occurs only in extended times, whereas Allah creates by "Be" and it is, so how do you strike the lesser similitude when to Him belongs the highest similitude beyond being perceived. There are in the verse discussions:

The first discussion: The Mu'tazilah said: this verse indicates that the non-existent is a thing, because He says to what He intends: "Be" and it is, so before the saying to it, "Be," it is not, and in that state it is a thing, since He said: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing﴾. The answer: this is an explanation of the non-failure of the thing to be when His intention is attached to it. His saying "idha" (when) conveys the notion of time and moment, and the verse indicates that the intended thing is a thing at the moment the intention is attached to it, and there is no indication in it that it is a thing before the time when He intends. Then what they mentioned does not arise, for the thing at the moment the intention is attached to it is an existing thing which He does not intend at one time and which exists at another time, but rather it exists at the time of the attachment of the intention. So the thing is the existent, not the non-existent. It is not said: how does He intend the existent while it is existent, so that this would be bringing into being what exists? We say: this difficulty belongs to the rational matters, and we answer it in its place. Our purpose here is only to refute their clinging to the wording, and it has become clear that what is understood from this speech is that He intends that which is a thing when He intends, and there is nothing in the verse that when He intends what was already a thing before the attachment of the intention.

The second discussion: The Karramiyyah said: God has a created will, by the proof of His saying: ﴿when He intends﴾, and the indication of this is from two matters:

The first: that He made the will to have a time, for "idha" is a temporal adverb, and everything temporal is originated.

The second: that He, the Exalted, linked His will to His saying: ﴿Be﴾, and His saying "Be" is linked to the existence of the thing and its occurrence, for He, the Exalted, said: ﴿and it is﴾ with the fa' of sequence, but the existence is originated, and what precedes the originated is linked to it and is originated.

The philosophers agreed with them on this difficulty from another aspect, saying: His will is linked to His command, and His command is linked to the existence, but His will is eternal, so the existence is eternal, and so God's creatures are eternal. The answer of the misguided to clinging to the wording is that what is understood from His saying: ﴿when He intends﴾ linguistically is "when His will is attached to the thing," because His saying "arada" (He intended) is a past verb, and when the word "idha" enters upon the past, it makes it mean the future. And we say: the notion of our saying "arada" and "yuridu" (intends) and "alima" (knew) and "ya'lamu" (knows) may admit occurrence, but we say that for Allah, the Exalted, there is an eternal attribute which is the will, and when that attribute is attached to a thing we say "arada" and "yuridu," and before the attachment we do not say "arada," but we say: He has a will and He is willing by it. Let us strike an example for weak understandings, so that what occurs in foolish imaginings may vanish. We say: our saying "so-and-so is a tailor" means that he has the craft of sewing. If it were not valid for us to say that he sewed the garment of Zayd or sews the garment of Zayd, it would not follow that our saying "he is a tailor" in the sense that he has a craft by which he is so described when he uses that craft on the garment of Zayd in a past time, having sewn his garment, and by which he is so described when he uses that craft on the garment of Zayd in a future time, he will sew his garment. And to Allah belongs the highest similitude. Understand that the will is a fixed matter: if it is attached to the existence of a thing we say "arada wujudahu," that is, "yuridu wujudahu" (He wills its existence). And when you know this, it is in meaning from the speech of the People of the Sunnah: the attachment of the will is originated, and by what we have mentioned the answer to both groups has come out.

The third discussion: The Mu'tazilah and the Karramiyyah said: the speech of God is letters, sound, and originated; because His saying "Be" is speech, and "Be" consists of two letters, and a letter is of sound, and it follows from this that His speech consists of letters and sounds. As for its being originated, it is for the two aspects previously mentioned:

The first: that it is temporal.

The second: that it is linked to the existence, and the existence is originated.

The answer is known from what we have mentioned, because speech is an attribute which, when attached to a thing, you say "qala" (he said) and "yaqulu" (he says), so the attachment of address is originated, while the speech is eternal. So His saying, the Exalted: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ contains attachment and relation, because His saying, the Exalted: ﴿says to it﴾ with the lam of relation is explicit in attachment. We say: His saying to the originated thing is originated, because it is with attachment; what is eternal is His saying and His speech, not with attachment. Every eternal and originated thing, when you consider their totality, you do not find both in the pre-eternity; rather you find both together in what never ceases, so it has the meaning of origination; but the unqualified expression is misleading. So reflect deeply, and do not say: "the totality is originated" without stating your intended meaning, for this may be understood to mean that the whole is originated. Rather, make the indication precise and perform the worship well, and say: one side of the totality is eternal and the other is originated, and the other was not with it in pre-eternity. As for His saying "Be" being of letters, we say: speech is applied to two meanings:

The first: what is with the speaker.

The second: what is with the hearer. Then one of them is applied to it as being the other, and from this certain benefits appear.

As for the explanation of what we have mentioned: when a person says to another, "I have a speech which I want to tell you tomorrow," then the hearer comes to him tomorrow and asks him about the speech that was with him yesterday, and he says to him: "I want you to attend with me today." This speech the speaker described as having been with you yesterday, and it was not with the hearer; then it came to be with the hearer by letters and sound, and he describes it as: "What you heard is what was with me." Every intelligent person knows that the sound was not with the speaker yesterday, nor the letters, because the speech that was with him could be expressed in Arabic, so it would have letters, and could be expressed in Persian, so it would have other letters, while the speech that was with him and which he promised is one, and the letters are different and many. So the meaning of his saying "this was not with me" is that this conveys to you what was with me, and this too is a figure of speech, because what was with him has not moved to the hearer; rather, the hearer came to know it and it came to be with him as knowledge derived from hearing or sight, in reading, writing, or gesture. When you know this, the speech that is with God and is His attribute is not letters, as has become clear, while what comes to be with the hearer is letters and sound, and one of them is the other for the meaning we have mentioned and the broadening of the application. So when He, the Exalted, says: ﴿says to it﴾, there come to be a speaker and a hearer, and He considered it from the side of the hearer, because the existence of the act from the hearer is for that saying; so He expressed it by the kaf and the nun, which occur in the hearer, and by which the sought thing comes into being.

And when you know this, it is in meaning from the speech of the People of the Sunnah: the attachment of the will is originated, and by what we have mentioned the answer to both groups has come out.

The third discussion: The Mu'tazilah and the Karramiyyah said: the speech of God is letters, sound, and originated; because His saying "Be" is speech, and "Be" consists of two letters, and a letter is of sound, and it follows from this that His speech consists of letters and sounds. As for its being originated, it is for the two aspects previously mentioned:

The first: that it is temporal.

The second: that it is linked to the existence, and the existence is originated.

The answer is known from what we have mentioned, because speech is an attribute which, when attached to a thing, you say "qala" (he said) and "yaqulu" (he says), so the attachment of address is originated, while the speech is eternal. So His saying, the Exalted: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ contains attachment and relation, because His saying, the Exalted: ﴿says to it﴾ with the lam of relation is explicit in attachment. We say: His saying to the originated thing is originated, because it is with attachment; what is eternal is His saying and His speech, not with attachment. Every eternal and originated thing, when you consider their totality, you do not find both in the pre-eternity; rather you find both together in what never ceases, so it has the meaning of origination; but the unqualified expression is misleading. So reflect deeply, and do not say: "the totality is originated" without stating your intended meaning, for this may be understood to mean that the whole is originated. Rather, make the indication precise and perform the worship well, and say: one side of the totality is eternal and the other is originated, and the other was not with it in pre-eternity. As for His saying "Be" being of letters, we say: speech is applied to two meanings:

The first: what is with the speaker.

The second: what is with the hearer. Then one of them is applied to it as being the other, and from this certain benefits appear.

As for the explanation of what we have mentioned: when a person says to another, "I have a speech which I want to tell you tomorrow," then the hearer comes to him tomorrow and asks him about the speech that was with him yesterday, and he says to him: "I want you to attend with me today." This speech the speaker described as having been with you yesterday, and it was not with the hearer; then it came to be with the hearer by letters and sound, and he describes it as: "What you heard is what was with me." Every intelligent person knows that the sound was not with the speaker yesterday, nor the letters, because the speech that was with him could be expressed in Arabic, so it would have letters, and could be expressed in Persian, so it would have other letters, while the speech that was with him and which he promised is one, and the letters are different and many. So the meaning of his saying "this was not with me" is that this conveys to you what was with me, and this too is a figure of speech, because what was with him has not moved to the hearer; rather, the hearer came to know it and it came to be with him as knowledge derived from hearing or sight, in reading, writing, or gesture. When you know this, the speech that is with God and is His attribute is not letters, as has become clear, while what comes to be with the hearer is letters and sound, and one of them is the other for the meaning we have mentioned and the broadening of the application. So when He, the Exalted, says: ﴿says to it﴾, there come to be a speaker and a hearer, and He considered it from the side of the hearer, because the existence of the act from the hearer is for that saying; so He expressed it by the kaf and the nun, which occur in the hearer, and by which the sought thing comes into being.

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿So glorified is He in whose hand is the dominion of all things, and to Him you will be returned.﴾

When the oneness of God and the resurrection had been established, and they denied them and claimed that other than God are gods, God, exalted and far removed from having partners, said: ﴿in whose hand is the dominion of all things﴾. Everything belongs to Him, so how could what is owned be a partner to the owner? And they said that resurrection would not happen, so He said: ﴿and to Him you will be returned﴾, as a refutation of them on both matters. We have already mentioned what relates to grammar in His words "subhan" (glory), meaning: glorify (with the glorification of) the One, or glorify, (you) who are in the heavens and the earth, the glorification of the One. ﴿Fa-subhan﴾ (so glorified) is a term (ʿalam) for glorification (tasbih), and tasbih is tanzih (declaring God free of imperfection and of partners). Malakut (dominion) is an intensive form of mulk (sovereignty), like rahamut (mercy) and rahabut (awe), and it is of the pattern fa'alul or fa'alut, about which there is discussion; and whoever says it is fa'alul has made it attached to that pattern.

Then the Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed, everything has a heart, and the heart of the Qur'an is Ya-Sin." Al-Ghazali said concerning it: this is because faith's soundness lies in acknowledging the gathering (hashr), and the gathering is established in this surah in the most eloquent manner, so he made it the heart of the Qur'an for that reason. Fakhr al-Din al-Razi (may God have mercy on him) approved of it; I heard him invoking mercy upon him because of this statement.

It may be said that this surah contains nothing but the establishment of the three foundations with the strongest proofs. Its beginning is the explanation of prophethood in His words: ﴿Indeed, you are among the messengers﴾ [Ya-Sin: 3], and its proof is what He placed before it in His words: ﴿By the wise Qur'an﴾ [Ya-Sin: 2], and what He placed after it in His words: ﴿that you may warn a people﴾. Its conclusion is the explanation of oneness and the gathering in His words: ﴿So glorified is He in whose hand is the dominion of all things﴾, which points to tawhid, and His words: ﴿and to Him you will be returned﴾, which point to the gathering. There is nothing in this surah except these three foundations, their proofs, and their reward. Whoever acquires this much of the Qur'an has acquired the share of the heart, which is the assent (tasdiq) of the inner heart.

As for the function of the tongue, which is speech, it is as in His words: ﴿O you who believe, fear God and speak words of directness﴾ [al-Ahzab: 70], and His words: ﴿And who is better in speech﴾ [Fussilat: 33], and His words: ﴿with the firm word﴾ [Ibrahim: 27], ﴿and He made them hold to the word of piety﴾ [al-Fath: 26], and ﴿To Him ascends the good word﴾ [Fatir: 10], and others from outside this surah. The function of the limbs is action, as in His words: ﴿So establish prayer and give zakat﴾ [al-Hajj: 78], and His words: ﴿And do not approach fornication﴾ [al-Isra: 32], ﴿and do not kill the soul﴾ [al-An'am: 151], and His words: ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 51], also from outside this surah. Since this surah contains nothing but actions of the heart and nothing else, he called it "heart." For this reason, it is reported in traditions that the Prophet ﷺ recommended reciting Ya-Sin to one who is near death and reciting it at his head; because at that time the tongue is weak in strength and the outward limbs have lost their structure, but the heart has turned toward God and withdrawn from everything else, so what increases the strength of his heart is recited at his head, and his assent to the three foundations is strengthened, and it is a cure for him. The secrets of the words of God and the words of the Messenger of God ﷺ are known only to God and His Messenger. What we have mentioned is conjecture that we do not affirm with certainty, and we hope that God will have mercy on us, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful.

The exegesis of this surah is complete, and praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, and may God bless our master Muhammad and his pure family.
